statement: The guide took the coastal route rather than the usual road; the party was the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Amir ibn Fuhayrah and the guide.
notes: Machine-checked ('the guide led them along the sea-shore'). The description of the usual road and the little-used tracks is from the Seerah.

statement: Abu Bakr's account to Azib: they travelled the night and the next day until noon; a rock with shade; he prepared a place and a fur for the Prophet to sleep; a shepherd came; he had him clean the udder and his hands, cooled the milk with water; 'Drink, Messenger of Allah'; he drank until Abu Bakr was pleased.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against both narrations.

statement: Suraqah's narration: a man reported figures on the coast; Suraqah denied it was them, went home, had his horse readied behind a hillock, left by the back; the horse stumbled; he drew lots and got the answer he disliked, and rode on.
notes: Machine-checked against the full text of Bukhari 3906. 'He wanted the reward for himself' is the evident sense of the narration, stated by the commentators.

statement: He heard the Prophet reciting, not turning, while Abu Bakr looked back often; the horse's forelegs sank to the knees; he drew lots again with the same result.

He called out offering safety; thought the Prophet's cause would prevail; told them of the reward and Quraysh's plans; offered provisions which they declined; the Prophet said 'keep our matter hidden'; Amir ibn Fuhayrah wrote him a guarantee on leather.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked. The promise of the bracelets of Kisra is not in this narration and is not narrated.

statement: Anas: at the beginning of the day he was an enemy of the Prophet and at its end a protector.
Anas: Abu Bakr was known along the road and the Prophet was not; asked who the man with him was, Abu Bakr would say 'this man shows me the way', meaning the way of good.
notes: Machine-checked. That Abu Bakr was known from trading journeys is the commentators' explanation.

statement: Urwah: they met az-Zubayr in a caravan of Muslim merchants returning from Syria; he gave the Prophet and Abu Bakr white garments; they were seen in white emerging from the mirage.
notes: Machine-checked. The story of Umm Ma'bad's tent is not narrated; its chains are disputed.
